outcome: Perioperative change in maternal hemoglobin levels
cohort: 98 women with singleton gestations undergoing primary scheduled cesarean section at term
finding: Delayed cord clamping (DCC) resulted in significantly higher maternal blood loss but no significant differences in secondary outcomes, including duration of cesarean section and neonatal data.
mod_finding: This study found that delayed umbilical cord clamping resulted in statistically significantly higher maternal blood loss compared to early cord clamping in scheduled cesarean sections.
